sources.title: M. W. Davis, The Geometry and Topology of Coxeter Groups, first-edition author manuscript (2007-2008)
sources.locator: Sections 7.3-7.4, printed pp. 128-132; section 12.1-12.3, printed pp. 231-236; section 13.2, printed pp. 260-262; Appendix I.1-I.7, printed pp. 499-523. The rest of the 600-page manuscript was not reread for this batch.

contents.name: Definition 7.3.1 and Examples 7.3.2: Coxeter polytopes C_W(d) = conv(Wx); C_2 gives an interval, the dihedral group of order 2m gives a 2m-gon, regular when x is equidistant from the walls
Lemma 7.3.3: the correspondence w -> wx gives a poset isomorphism WS = (face poset of C) for finite W
Proposition 7.3.4: the cell structure on Sigma (vertex set W, 1-skeleton the Cayley graph, cells the spherical cosets wW_T, vertex link L)
Lemma 7.3.5: Sigma is simply connected, via the Cayley 2-complex and cellular approximation
Example 7.4.1 and Example 7.4.5: for m_st = infinity the nerve is discrete and Sigma is a regular k-valent tree; for k = 2 the real line cellulated by intervals
Example 7.4.2: 2-dimensional Sigma, one 2m-gon per edge of the nerve and the condition 1/m_1 + 1/m_2 + 1/m_3 <= 1 on 3-circuits
contents.reason: The rank-three diagram conditions for a 2-dimensional Davis complex are not consumed by any item of this pair; the companion computes the link angles of A2, affine A2 and the universal case, and the 2-dimensional classification is left to a future page.

contents.name: Section 7.5: fixed posets F(T) and fixed subspaces of spherical special subgroups (Lemma 7.5.1, Corollaries 7.5.2-7.5.3, Lemma 7.5.4)
contents.reason: The fixed-subspace cell complexes of arbitrary spherical W_T are not consumed by the contracted items: the finite-subgroup theorem uses the point-stabilizer formula of the cellulation plus the CAT(0) fixed point theorem, and the companion records only the rank-one and top-rank examples.

contents.name: Section 12.1: the piecewise Euclidean cell structure of Sigma; Lemma 12.1.1: the vertex link is the spherical simplex with vertex set the inward normals and cosine matrix the cosine matrix of (W,S), independent of d
Theorem 12.2.1 (Gromov): the right-angled cubical structure is CAT(0), and the CAT(-1) criterion via the no-square condition
contents.reason: The right-angled case is a special case of the general Moussong theorem scaffolded here, and the CAT(-1)/no-square refinement is not part of this pair's scope; no separate right-angled item is promised by the design.

contents.name: Lemma 12.3.1 and Corollary 12.3.2: the nerve of a Coxeter system has simplices of size >= pi/2 and is metric flag, hence CAT(1)
Theorem 12.3.3 (Moussong): Sigma with its natural piecewise Euclidean structure is CAT(0)
Theorem 12.3.4(i): every finite subgroup of W is conjugate to a finite subgroup of a spherical special subgroup, via isotropy subgroups and the Bruhat-Tits fixed point theorem
Theorem 12.3.4(ii)-(iv) and Theorem 12.3.5: finite model for EW, solvable subgroups virtually free abelian, virtually abelian groups finite or affine
contents.reason: These consequences (proper-action models, solvability and virtual abelianness) require their own prerequisites and are explicitly excluded from this pair by the owner direction, which forbids appending flat-torus, automaticity and related theorems without separate closure.

contents.name: Section 12.4, 12.6-12.8: visual boundary, the CAT(-1) criterion, free abelian subgroups, relative hyperbolization
contents.reason: None of these results is consumed by the contracted items of this pair; the boundary and hyperbolicity material belongs to later pages of the track with their own girth and hyperbolicity prerequisites.

contents.name: Appendix I.2: Definition I.2.1 (CAT(kappa)); Theorem I.2.5 (uniqueness of geodesics); Theorem I.2.6 (a complete CAT(0) space is contractible, with the geodesic contraction h(x,t)); Theorem I.2.7 (Gromov's Cartan-Hadamard theorem); Proposition I.2.10 (the center of a bounded set in a complete CAT(0) space); Theorem I.2.11 (Bruhat-Tits fixed point theorem); Proposition I.2.12 (fixed point sets are convex, CAT(0) and contractible when nonempty); Lemma I.2.15 (the squared-distance form of the CAT(0) inequality)

Appendix I.3: piecewise constant curvature polyhedra, geometric links, Proposition I.3.4 (finitely many shapes gives a complete geodesic space) and Theorem I.3.5 (curvature <= kappa if and only if the vertex links are CAT(1))

Appendix I.5: Lemma I.5.1 (edge lengths of a spherical simplex via positive definiteness); Lemmas I.5.11-I.5.12 (links of simplices of size >= pi/2 again have size >= pi/2); Lemma I.6.1 (Gromov's Lemma)

Appendix I.7: Definition I.7.1 (metric flag complex); Lemma I.7.3 (links of a metric flag complex are metric flag); Lemma I.7.4 (Moussong's Lemma: CAT(1) if and only if metric flag); Lemma I.7.5 (Bowditch's short-loop criterion, proof sketch); the nerve of a normalized almost negative matrix; Lemma I.7.6 (extra largeness)
Section 13.2: spherical parabolic subgroups are precisely the isotropy subgroups of Sigma
Lemma 13.2.3: the fixed set of a finite subgroup is the fixed set of a spherical parabolic
contents.reason: The approved item proves finite-subgroup fixed points and containment in a spherical parabolic, as in Theorem 12.3.4(i), together with the exact point-isotropy formula supplied by the preceding Davis-cellulation theorem. Equality of fixed sets with a containing spherical parabolic is not claimed or used; this separate stronger result is not an additional promise of the selected item.

sources.title: M. W. Davis and G. Moussong, Notes on nonpositively curved polyhedra, Turan Workshop notes (1998/1999)
sources.locator: Sections 1.2-1.6, printed pp. 6-15; section 2.2-2.3, printed pp. 19-24; sections 6.3-6.7, printed pp. 36-41. Sections 3-5 (cubical examples, hyperbolization) and 7-10 (Minkowski hypersurfaces, L2-homology) were read only at the level of the table of contents.

contents.name: Definition 1.4.2-1.4.5 and Proposition 1.4.4: CAT(kappa) inequalities, comparison triangles, Aleksandrov angles and curvature <= kappa
Theorem 1.5.2 (Gromov's Cartan-Hadamard theorem) and Corollary 1.5.3 (a complete nonpositively curved geodesic space is aspherical)
Section 1.5: convexity of the distance function on a CAT(0) space
Section 1.6: the cone on a CAT(1) space and its metric (Berestovskii's theorem)
Section 2.2-2.3: polyhedra of piecewise constant curvature, links, Gromov's Lemma for all-right complexes
Theorem 6.4.1, Lemma 6.4.3: for any finitely generated Coxeter group there is a CAT(0) piecewise Euclidean complex Sigma with proper action and compact quotient, and Sigma = U(W,K)
Lemma 6.5.1: W is finite if and only if the cosine matrix is positive definite
Lemma 6.5.5: WS is the face poset of the Coxeter cell and Lk(v,Sigma) = the dual fundamental simplex
Section 6.6: the piecewise Euclidean cell structure on Sigma and the reduction of CAT(0) to the CAT(1)-ness of the vertex links
Example 6.7.3: the nerve of a Coxeter group has simplices of size >= pi/2, edge lengths pi - pi/m_ij, and is metric flag
Lemma 6.7.4 (Moussong's Lemma): a piecewise spherical complex whose cells are simplices of size >= pi/2 is CAT(1) if and only if it is metric flag, with the Bowditch short-loop proof sketch
Corollary 6.7.5: Sigma is CAT(0)
Lemma 6.7.6 (Bowditch's criterion): a compact space of curvature <= 1 in which every nonconstant closed curve of length < 2pi is shrinkable is CAT(1)
Section 6.8: when Sigma is CAT(-1): extra largeness, Lemmas 6.8.1-6.8.2 and the word-hyperbolicity corollary
contents.reason: The CAT(-1) and word-hyperbolicity material is explicitly excluded from this pair's scope by the owner direction and requires the extra-large girth hypotheses and the hyperbolicity page, neither of which is scaffolded here.

sources.locator: PDF pp. 8-15 (Definitions 2.4-2.7, Definitions 2.15-2.18, Theorem 2.19 and Proposition 2.21). The remaining slides (Artin groups and references, PDF pp. 16-19) were read only at the level of their headings.

contents.name: Definitions 2.5-2.6: spherical subsets, the poset S and the nerve L(W,S)
Definition 2.18 and Proposition 2.21: the geometric realization of a poset, Sigma = U(W,K), and K = Sigma/W
Theorem 2.19(ii),(iii),(iv): one cell per spherical subset, the 0-skeleton is W and the 1-skeleton is the Cayley graph
Theorem 2.19(vii),(viii): the induced piecewise Euclidean metric on Sigma is CAT(0) (Gromov, Moussong) and Sigma is contractible
Theorem 2.19(ix),(x): the action is proper because isotropy subgroups are conjugate to spherical special subgroups, and the quotient is compact
Theorem 2.19(vi) and Example 2.17: in the right-angled case each Coxeter cell is a cube, and (Z/2)^n gives the cube
Theorem 2.19(xi) and slides on Coxeter zonotopes: for finite W, Sigma is a Coxeter zonotope (the permutohedron for type A)
Theorem 2.20 and the Artin-group slides (PDF pp. 15-16): the reflection group trick application, K(A,1) problem, RAAGs
contents.reason: The Artin group and reflection-trick material is not consumed by any item of this pair and belongs to the Artin/Hecke track, which has its own pages and supplier contracts in this run.

contents.name: II.2.4-2.6: the nearest-point projection onto a complete convex subset, its convexity properties and the homotopy from the identity to the projection
Proposition II.2.7: the centre of a bounded set of radius < D_kappa/2 in a complete CAT(kappa) space, with the Cauchy-sequence proof (the kappa = 0 case used here)
Corollary II.2.8(1): a finite group of isometries, or a group of isometries with a bounded orbit, of a complete CAT(0) space has a nonempty convex fixed-point set
Theorem II.4.1 and II.4.8-II.4.12: the Cartan-Hadamard theorem for metric spaces (complete, connected, simply connected, locally CAT(0) implies CAT(0))
Theorem II.5.20 (Gromov) and Lemma II.5.21 (Moussong's Lemma in the metric flag form)
Chapter II.6, PDF p. 253: R-trees, elliptic and semi-simple isometries
Chapter II.12, PDF pp. 414-415: the Davis complex of a Coxeter group as the geometric realization of the poset of spherical subsets, contractible, with proper action
Chapters II.10-II.11: buildings, the Cartan fixed point theorem for Euclidean buildings, and symmetric spaces
contents.reason: The building and symmetric-space material is not used by this pair; the Coxeter-specific fixed point statement is supplied by the CAT(0) circumcenter route and the in-run cell-stabilizer theorem instead.

contents.name: Section 11-13: the main construction K(W), the cells F_{T,U}, and the characteristic maps
Formula (5): lk(F_{T,U}, K(W)) = lk(N(A_U),N(A)) * S^{|T|-1} for the link of a cell
Theorem 14.1: for every Coxeter group there is a contractible E-complex K(W) of curvature <= 0 on which W acts effectively, properly and with compact quotient
Remark 14.2: K(W) is a convex polyhedron for finite W, a regular 2m-gon for the dihedral group, and a Euclidean tessellation for affine W
Corollaries 15.1-15.2 and Chapter 4 (Theorem 17.1, the hyperbolicity characterization)
contents.reason: The solvability consequences and the CAT(-1)/hyperbolicity characterization depend on Selberg's lemma and extra-large girth hypotheses and are excluded from this pair by the owner direction.

contents.name: Section 2: almost negative matrices, the nerve complex N(A), and Lemma 2.1 (the link of a simplex is the nerve of the link matrix, with lk(I,A) again almost negative)
Section 2: the Moussong metric on the Davis complex and Proposition 2.4 (simply connected, proper cocompact action, the link of a simplex is isometric to lk(B_I,N(A)))
Theorem 3.1: a simply connected complete metric space is CAT(0) if and only if it is locally CAT(0)
Propositions 3.3-3.4: the nerve of an almost negative matrix is CAT(1) if and only if its girth and the girths of its links are >= 2pi, and Moussong's girth computation for Coxeter nerves
Sections 3-4: the gap in Moussong's Lemmas 9.5, 9.7, 9.11 and the workaround for the Gromov-hyperbolicity characterization
contents.reason: The gap analysis and its repair concern the hyperbolicity characterization, not the CAT(0) theorem used here; the CAT(0) part is explicitly recorded by the author as problem-free and is what this batch consumes.
